- resolving maps to an existing version or creates one and marks the entry resolved via the Vehicles context API
- resolution/import writes audit entries; newest-first ordering uses a desc: :id tiebreaker

title: Rating studio: per-code CSV import with row-error preview
description: Broker barèmes arrive as spreadsheets and hand-typing jsonb is error-prone, so each table code needs a CSV round-trip with a template and previewed row errors (§10.4). Extend the rating studio with per-code CSV import: template download (headers per code), upload via Phoenix.LiveView uploads, parse with NimbleCSV, map rows to the code's jsonb shape, and render a preview table with per-row validation errors before commit. Commit writes a new `draft` version (never published) through Sahla.Rating and audits the import.
design: NimbleCSV, all-or-nothing commit. Reuse the editor's validator. Preview list empty-state outside any stream container.
acceptance_criteria:
- template download returns the correct headers for the selected table code
- malformed rows are listed with row number + reason; valid rows preview parsed values
- import is all-or-nothing: blocked entirely if any row is invalid (asserted in test)
- a successful import creates a draft version whose data equals the parsed grid
- oversized or non-CSV uploads are rejected (size + content-type checks)

title: Build CSV exports for leads, quotes and conversions
description: Finance and the partner broker need periodic CSV extracts for reconciliation and commission reporting (§10.11). Add SahlaWeb.Admin.ExportsController serving streamed CSV of leads, quotes and conversions filtered by period, restricted to the finance role (ops/superadmin allowed). Reuse the dashboard/leads read modules for the underlying queries; stream rows to avoid loading everything in memory; audit each export. Columns expose non-PII projections plus hashed identifiers where needed.
design: Never emit raw phone/CIN in CSV — hashed or masked projections only (Lessons, PII). Stream via Repo.stream inside Repo.transaction. Period parsing shared with dashboard metrics. Authorization via the admin-auth role plug.
acceptance_criteria:
- Three exports (leads, quotes, conversions) generate valid CSV for a given period
- Only finance/ops/superadmin roles can access the export routes; others get 403
- Rows are streamed (Repo.stream in a transaction), not materialized fully in memory
- Exported columns avoid raw PII, using hashed identifiers/projections where applicable
- Each export writes an audit_entries record (who/what/period)
- Tests assert CSV shape, role authorization, and audit logging

title: Add SLA badges, working-hours awareness and agent presence
description: Operational safety rails: surface stale leads and stop two agents phoning the same person (§7.3, §10.2). Add an SLA badge helper that turns a new/untouched lead red after >15 min of elapsed working time (Africa/Casablanca), computed against configurable working hours from settings. Wire SahlaWeb.Presence so the kanban and lead detail show which agent is currently viewing a lead. Badges render on kanban cards and detail header; presence avatars update live.
design: Reuse the working-hours helper across auto-assignment and callback slots. Presence via Phoenix.Presence tracked in the LiveView. Badge color is a computed assign; no timers leaking PII. Timezone fixed to Africa/Casablanca via ex_cldr.
acceptance_criteria:
- A nouveau lead untouched > 15 min of working time renders a red SLA badge; touched leads clear it
- SLA elapsed time counts only configured working hours, not overnight/closed periods
- Working hours and SLA threshold are read from settings, not hardcoded
- Opening a lead registers presence; other admins see the viewing agent within ~1s
- Leaving the lead clears the presence indicator
- Tests cover the working-hours SLA calculation and presence join/leave tracking

title: Emit offers-page telemetry events
description: The analytics plan needs server-side funnel events to measure the results stage (§11 event list, §10.1 dashboard). Emit :telemetry events from OffresLive and RappelLive: offers_viewed (on view), offer_selected (on détails/CTA/compare selection), and callback_booked (on lead creation). Attach non-PII measurements/metadata — offer count, insurer, formula, badge, and a hashed token — feeding the server-side funnel events table and PromEx. Centralize the event names and metadata shape so emitters across the epic stay consistent.
design: Lessons/PII: never emit raw phone or external payloads — use safe projections and the phone_hash pattern. Event names/metadata shape defined here; callback-flow reuses the callback_booked definition.
acceptance_criteria:
- offers_viewed is emitted once per page view on mount
- offer_selected is emitted on détails/CTA/compare selection with offer metadata
- callback_booked is emitted on successful lead creation
- Events carry non-PII metadata only (no raw phone; token is hashed)
- Tests attach a :telemetry test handler and assert each event fires

title: Render server-side devis PDF of selected offers
description: The step-4 email incentive promises "recevez vos devis en PDF" (§5.2), a lever for capturing email and re-engaging leads. Build a server-side PDF export of the user's selected offers in SahlaWeb.DevisPDF: render a print-optimized HTML view (offer breakdowns from the rating_run, the indicative-prices disclaimer, ACAPS placeholder) and convert it to a PDF server-side without any Node runtime dependency. Return the PDF bytes so Notifications can attach it to the transactional email (email sending itself is owned by notifications). Output must be reproducible from the immutable rating_run snapshot.
design: PDF library choice needs dependency approval (avoid hackney per Lessons; avoid Node). Candidates: Typst port, wkhtmltopdf binary, or ChromicPDF (headless chrome) — flag trade-offs, decide in impl. Store no raw PII; render from safe projections of the snapshot.
acceptance_criteria:
- Generates a PDF of the selected offers including breakdowns, disclaimer and ACAPS placeholder
- Rendered server-side with no Node runtime dependency and deterministic from the rating_run
- FR/AR content supported with RTL for AR; prices tabular in Western digits
- Returns PDF bytes suitable for email attachment; a test asserts a non-empty valid PDF header
- Indicative-price labeling present on the document (compliance)

title: Build simulator core API for draft-vs-published premium diffs
description: Governance (§9.2) requires previewing premium impact before publishing a draft table, so provide the pure core API (the admin UI on top is admin-studio). Build Rating.Simulator with run_profile(inputs, draft_tables) and run_batch(personas, draft_tables) that compute offers against a draft table set overlaid on the current published set, returning per-insurer/formula diffs (old, new, delta, pct). Resolve the published baseline via table-resolution and overlay only the draft code(s) under test without publishing anything. The golden persona set is reusable as a batch source. The API is read-only and returns a plain struct for the admin-studio LiveView to render.
design: Overlay merges the draft into the load_all map. Admin UI/CSV screens are admin-studio (not owned). §9.2 simulator.
acceptance_criteria:
- run_profile returns paired old/new premiums plus delta and pct per insurer/formula
- A draft table overlay affects only its own code(s); other codes use the current published rows
- run_batch over the persona set returns an aggregate plus per-persona diffs
- The API is read-only — test asserts no rows are written and no publish side effects occur
- An unpublished draft is never used by Engine.run for real quotes, only via the simulator
close_reason: Built Sahla.Rating.Simulator — the pure, read-only draft-vs-published premium preview (§9.2). run_profile(inputs, draft_tables, opts) overlays draft rate tables (a %{code => data} map) onto the published baseline (Tables.load_all/1, or opts[:baseline] injected) via Map.merge — so codes NOT in the draft keep their published rows — runs BOTH the baseline and overlaid sets through the same pure Rating.Engine, and pairs offers by {insurer_slug, formula} into %Simulator.Diff{insurer, formula, old_centimes, new_centimes, delta_centimes, pct} (nil-safe when a draft makes an offer appear/disappear; pct = delta/old). run_batch(personas, draft_tables, opts) resolves the baseline+overlay once and maps run_profile over the golden persona set, returning %{aggregate: %{personas, lines, total_old/new/delta_centimes, avg_pct}, personas: [%{inputs, diffs}]}. No branch writes to the DB (only Tables.load_all, an ETS read). 5 tests: empty draft → zero deltas; draft → old/new/delta/pct per line; OVERLAY ISOLATION (draft touching only wafa's positioning changes wafa, leaves axa's premium identical); batch aggregate + per-persona; READ-ONLY (seeds a published set, runs the real load_all path, asserts Table count unchanged and no row left non-published — no publish/archive side effects). Admin-studio LiveView/CSV is out of scope (not owned) and consumes these structs. Full suite 406 pass, credo clean (816), prod compiles.

title: Add property tests for rating monotonicity and invariants
description: The §9.2 invariants must hold across the whole input space, so encode them as StreamData property tests over Rating.Engine.run. Generate valid random inputs and tables and assert: monotonicity (more at-fault claims never make an offer cheaper; higher fiscal_power never lowers premium_rc; higher vehicle value never lowers an AC-type RC line), no negative breakdown lines, total equals the sum of the breakdown, an EVCAT line is always present, and every total is rounded to a whole dirham. These properties complement the golden fixtures by covering ranges no persona enumerates.
design: Pure engine makes properties cheap and flake-free. Fixed seed for reproducible CI. §9.2 property tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Property: increasing at_fault_claims_36m never lowers any offer total
- Property: increasing fiscal_power never lowers premium_rc
- Property: every breakdown line is ≥ 0 and total == Σ lines
- Property: an EVCAT line is present in every generated offer
- Each property runs ≥ 100 generated cases with a fixed CI seed

title: RTL correctness pass with logical-utility grep guard
description: Automatic RTL mirroring only works if the codebase uses logical utilities exclusively, so this pass enforces and verifies that discipline (§6.3). Audit all templates/components to use ms-/me-/ps-/pe-/text-start|end only, replacing any ml-/mr-/pl-/pr-/text-left|right. Add rtl:rotate-180 to directional icons (arrows, chevrons). Add a mix task or CI script (grep-based) that fails when a forbidden physical-direction class appears in HEEx, so regressions are caught. Visually verify key surfaces (layout, funnel card, offer card, overlays) mirror correctly under dir=rtl.
design: The grep guard is the durable safeguard — logical utilities are only as good as their enforcement. Not a central gate task; this is the RTL-specific check the Lessons call for. Coordinate with design-system components already using ms-/me-.
acceptance_criteria:
- No ml-/mr-/pl-/pr-/text-left/text-right classes remain in HEEx (grep guard passes clean)
- A mix task/CI script fails the build when a forbidden physical-direction class is introduced
- Directional icons carry rtl:rotate-180 and visibly flip under RTL
- Public layout, funnel card, offer card and overlays render correctly mirrored at dir=rtl
- The guard script is documented and self-tested against a deliberately bad sample

title: Quality-floor pass: a11y, 360px, reduced-motion, JS budget
description: The plan sets a hard quality floor the whole kit must clear, so this pass audits and fixes the component library and layouts against it (§6.4). Verify responsiveness down to 360px, visible keyboard focus rings on every interactive element, WCAG AA contrast for all token pairings (Majorelle/ink/teal/terracotta on sand/white), prefers-reduced-motion honored everywhere (star progress, skeletons, staged loader), and a total JS bundle under 120KB. Produce a short checklist artifact, fix violations in the components, and document contrast ratios for the token pairs actually used.
design: Terracotta is sparse/promo-only partly for contrast reasons — verify it never carries body text on sand. JS budget is protected by LiveView-first design and minimal hooks. This is an audit-and-fix pass, not new components.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every interactive component shows a visible focus ring at 360px and desktop widths
- Documented contrast ratios prove WCAG AA for all text/background token pairs in use
- prefers-reduced-motion disables all non-essential animation across the kit (verified per component)
- Production JS bundle measured < 120KB and the figure recorded
- No horizontal scroll or clipped content at 360px on the showcase covering all components

title: Add 404/500 error pages & static asset config
description: Users and monitors will hit missing/broken routes, so the app needs branded-neutral 404 and 500 pages instead of raw Plug fallbacks (§10, Appendix A controllers). Implement `SahlaWeb.ErrorHTML` (and ErrorJSON) rendering friendly 404 and 500 templates that reuse the base layout and pull any display name from Settings/gettext (no hardcoded brand). Ensure Endpoint uses these views in prod (debug_errors false) and that the 403 path from the authz plug renders here too. Confirm Plug.Static serves the mix-compiled tailwind/esbuild assets with long cache headers, and that the LiveView error/disconnect states degrade gracefully. Keep templates minimal and RTL-safe (logical utilities).
design: Templates use logical (ms-/me-) utilities so they survive the later RTL pass. Display name from Settings/gettext keeps brand TBD. 403 reuse avoids a bespoke forbidden page.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unknown routes render the 404 template (200-body, 404 status) in prod config, not a stack trace
- Raised server errors render the 500 template with debug_errors disabled in prod
- 403 responses from AdminAuthz render through the same error view
- ErrorJSON returns JSON error bodies for API/webhook content types
- Plug.Static serves compiled assets with cache_control headers; digested assets resolve
- ConnTest asserts 404 and 500 render the custom templates
close_reason: Implemented branded 403/404/500 error pages via SahlaWeb.ErrorHTML (§10, Appendix A). Explicit render/2 clauses for 403/404/500 render a self-contained page (inline styles, no asset-build or app-layout dependency, so a 500 from a broken pipeline/asset still renders cleanly), with copy via Gettext (FR) and brand from Settings.display_name/0 (ETS-backed, safe during a DB outage — never hardcoded). RTL-safe: dir attribute + logical margin-block/inline CSS. Other statuses fall back to the plain status message. The AdminAuthz plug's existing render('403.html') now resolves here. ErrorJSON unchanged — its fallback already returns %{errors:%{detail}} JSON for API/webhook content types. Verified acceptance: unknown route returns 404 with the branded template (ConnTest asserts status+body, not a stack trace); debug_errors is false in prod (only dev sets true); Plug.Static already serves compiled assets (static_paths + gzip) with default far-future cache-control on digested ?vsn requests; root layout already carries the LiveView phx-disconnected/phx-connected degrade-gracefully flash handlers. 7 error-view tests (branded 403/404/500 render, teapot fallback, endpoint 404), full suite 389 pass, credo clean, prod compiles.

title: Add telemetry, PromEx metrics, JSON logs & Sentry transport
description: Observability is required from day one for the single-VPS deploy (§7.3, §13.7). Wire a `SahlaWeb.Telemetry` supervisor exposing Phoenix/Ecto/LiveView/Oban/BEAM metrics, integrate PromEx to publish a Prometheus /metrics endpoint (scraped by Grafana Cloud), and configure structured JSON logging (a JSON logger formatter) so journald lines are machine-parseable. Integrate Sentry for exceptions including LiveView crashes — critically via a custom Finch-based transport, because Sentry's default client pulls hackney which conflicts with req/mint idna (Lessons). Read SENTRY_DSN from runtime env (Appendix B); Sentry is a no-op when the DSN is unset.
design: Custom Finch transport for Sentry is mandatory to keep hackney out (idna conflict). PromEx over raw telemetry_metrics_prometheus for batteries-included dashboards. JSON logs align with journald/Grafana ingestion (§13.7). Scrub PII (phone/CIN/tokens/raw payloads) from every Sentry event; Sentry stays a no-op without SENTRY_DSN.
acceptance_criteria:
- PromEx serves Prometheus metrics (BEAM memory, Ecto query time, LiveView mounts, Oban queue depth)
- Logs are emitted as structured JSON with request/trace metadata
- Sentry uses a custom Finch transport — mix deps.tree confirms no hackney is introduced
- SENTRY_DSN is read from runtime env; Sentry is inert (no crash) when DSN is absent
- A raised exception in a test/dev request is captured by the Sentry client (mocked transport)
- Telemetry supervisor starts in the tree without warnings

title: Tune Oban retention/pruning vs infinite job uniqueness
description: Notifications.Workers.{SMS,Email}Worker use unique: [keys: [:idempotency_key], period: :infinity]. That keeps completed oban_jobs rows around indefinitely for the uniqueness check (no Oban.Plugins.Pruner is configured). Correctness does NOT depend on it — the notifications_log.idempotency_key unique index + the settled?/no-op guard in Notifications.deliver/3 is the durable exactly-once backstop even if a job row is pruned or the period is bounded. Follow-up: either add Oban.Plugins.Pruner with a bounded uniqueness period (e.g. 7d) or accept unbounded retention, and add delivery observability (queue depth, failure-rate telemetry).
acceptance_criteria: Oban job retention has a deliberate policy; uniqueness period documented; delivery failure/queue telemetry emitted

title: Phase 2 kickoff gate: MVP launched + PMF signal
description: Feature-creep guard from §15: nothing outside the MVP list ships before the first 100 leads. This gate blocks all Phase 2 (Buy Online) engineering until (1) the public MVP launch happened (gate M6 closed), (2) the first-100-leads signal (or an explicit ops decision) is recorded, and (3) the CMI merchant contract and first binding-insurer partnership tracks are underway (§14 weeks 13-22). Closing this issue is a deliberate product decision — record the rationale and the chosen Phase 2 scope order in the close reason.
design: Exists so bd ready never surfaces Phase 2 work early. Do not close mechanically.
acceptance_criteria:
- gate M6 closed and the MVP is publicly live
- first-100-leads milestone (or explicit override decision) recorded
- CMI merchant contract + binding-insurer partnership status noted
- Phase 2 scope order agreed and recorded on close

title: Add optional GA4 marketing analytics integration
description: The marketing team may want GA4 alongside the MVP Plausible + server-side funnel events (§11 Analytics). Add an optional, settings-flagged GA4 integration: inject the GA4 tag via the layout (respecting cookie consent), and mirror the key server-side funnel events (funnel_step_completed, offers_viewed, offer_selected, otp_verified, lead_created, callback_booked) as GA4 Measurement Protocol events where a client tag isn't sufficient. Loading GA4 must be gated on marketing consent and the feature flag; it is off by default and adds no JS when disabled.
design: Consent-gated per Law 09-08/CNDP. Reuse existing funnel event taxonomy — do not fork event names. Measurement Protocol calls use Req/Finch. Off by default; Plausible remains primary.
acceptance_criteria:
- GA4 tag injected via the layout only when the feature flag is on AND marketing consent is granted; zero added JS when off
- Measurement ID comes from settings/env, never hard-coded; no PII is sent to GA4
- Key funnel events are mirrored consistently with the existing server-side event names
- Consent withdrawal stops GA4 loading/sending on subsequent page loads
- Tests/assertions confirm the tag is absent without consent and present with it

title: Prepare and file ACAPS full online-subscription dossier
description: Moving from a quote/advertising device to full online subscription legally requires filing the complete ACAPS dossier BEFORE Phase 2 launch, and re-notifying on any change (§3.2, §12 item 2). This is business/legal work: assemble the device URL, a detailed subscription-process walkthrough, CGV, consent mechanics, payment flow description, and data handling, aligned with Instruction P.IN.02/2022. File with ACAPS and obtain acknowledgement before enabling online payment/issuance in production. Establish the re-notification process for future changes. Gate the online-subscription feature flag on filing completion.
design: Human/legal deliverable — no code, but it hard-gates enabling CMI payment + issuance in production. Builds on phase0 device notification. Keep all legal texts in the CMS legal-text manager so changes are versioned and re-notifiable.
acceptance_criteria:
- Full dossier assembled: device URL, subscription-process walkthrough, CGV, consent mechanics, payment + data-handling descriptions
- Dossier aligns with ACAPS Instruction P.IN.02/2022 and is reviewed by insurance counsel before submission
- Dossier filed with ACAPS and acknowledgement recorded; online-subscription go-live is blocked until acknowledgement exists
- A documented re-notification process exists for any subsequent device modification
- The online-payment/subscription feature flag is only enabled in prod after filing is confirmed

title: Upgrade WhatsApp to Business API with templates
description: WhatsApp is a first-class channel in Morocco; Phase 2 upgrades from wa.me deep links to the Business API for templated devis, callback confirmations, and renewal reminders (§5.3, §11 WhatsApp). Add a `Notifications.WhatsApp` behaviour with a real adapter (Meta/360dialog/Twilio) and a deterministic Fake default. Manage approved message templates and their variables, an opt-in registry (consent + opt-out), and an inbound webhook (delivery/read receipts, replies) through a CSRF-exempt, signature-verified pipeline applied exactly-once. Secrets via runtime.exs env. Feature-flag gated so email/SMS/wa.me remain the fallback when off.
design: External-provider pattern (Lessons): behaviour + Fake default, config-swap, CSRF-exempt signature-verified webhook, exactly-once in a transaction. HTTP via Req/Finch, not hackney. Template approval is an operational flow tracked in settings/admin.
acceptance_criteria:
- Notifications.WhatsApp behaviour with a Fake default; real adapter selected via settings; secrets only from runtime.exs env
- Templated sends (devis/callback/renewal) use approved templates with variable substitution; each send logs to notifications_log
- Opt-in/opt-out registry is enforced before any send; opted-out contacts are suppressed and logged
- Inbound webhook is CSRF-exempt, signature-verified with secure_compare in the context, and status updates apply exactly-once (terminal = no-op)
- When the feature flag is off, callers transparently fall back to email/SMS/wa.me with no error
- Tests cover template send, opt-out suppression, webhook signature rejection, and exactly-once delivery updates

title: Add travel vertical incl. Schengen-visa insurance
description: Travel — especially Schengen-visa insurance — is a proven Moroccan traffic magnet (§4 Phase 2, §5.4 SEO). Add travel products (kind=voyage) with travel rate_tables (destination zone, trip duration, traveller count/age bands, coverage level), a travel funnel variant of DevisLive (destination, dates, travellers, purpose incl. Schengen), and offers rendering with visa-compliant coverage badges. Include a Schengen-specific option ensuring the minimum EUR 30,000 medical cover often required for visa. Add SEO content hooks (guide/landing) coordinated with content-seo. FR/AR throughout. Leads and admin flow unchanged.
design: Reuse the add-a-line pattern proven by moto. Schengen minimum cover is a config value in rate_tables, not hard-coded. Coordinate the SEO magnet page with content-seo. Engine remains table-driven and pure.
acceptance_criteria:
- kind=voyage products + versioned travel rate_tables (zone/duration/age/coverage) authored in the rating studio
- Travel funnel variant collects destination, dates, travellers, and Schengen purpose; validates dates (start<end, not past)
- A Schengen offer surfaces the required minimum medical coverage and flags visa-compliance clearly
- Travel quotes create leads and reuse offers page, OTP, and admin kanban unchanged
- All travel fields have FR + AR labels; a Schengen landing/guide hook is exposed for content-seo
- Tests cover travel rating from tables, Schengen coverage flag, date validation, and lead parity

title: Add moto vertical via the add-a-line pattern
description: Moto is the first non-auto vertical and validates the add-a-line pattern (§2 row 19, §4 Phase 2). Add moto products (Directory) with kind=moto, moto-specific rate_tables (rc_base bands, options, positioning) authored in the rating studio, and a moto funnel variant of DevisLive reusing step components with moto-appropriate fields (cylindrée/type instead of puissance fiscale nuances, moto usage). Results/offers, OTP, lead capture, and admin all flow through unchanged. Seed a minimal moto catalog. FR/AR labels for all new fields. Reuse the Quoting.Source resolver so binding moto offers work later.
design: Engine stays pure/table-driven — moto = new tables, not new code paths. Reuse funnel + results + notifications MVP infra. One-tap cards over native selects (Lessons). Author FR + AR catalogs, no empty msgids.
acceptance_criteria:
- Directory supports kind=moto products; moto rate_tables are versioned/publishable via the rating studio like auto
- A moto funnel variant reuses DevisLive step components with moto fields; one-tap option cards for small enums (no native select)
- Rating.Engine computes moto offers from moto tables with no branching business numbers in code
- Moto quotes create leads and flow through the same offers page, OTP, and admin kanban unchanged
- All new moto funnel fields have FR + AR gettext labels and RTL-correct layout
- Tests cover moto rating from tables, funnel completion, and lead creation parity with auto

title: Build referral/cashback program with fraud controls
description: Referral/cashback drives cheap acquisition and works well in Morocco but needs fraud controls (§2 row 13, §4 Phase 2). Add a `Referrals` context: per-user referral codes/links, referral records (referrer, referee quote/lead, status pending|qualified|paid, reward_centimes), and payout eligibility (reward only on a `gagné`/issued policy). Fraud controls: self-referral blocking (phone_hash/IP checks), velocity caps (Hammer), duplicate-device/phone detection, and manual finance review before payout. Surface referral status in the customer panel and a finance-role admin view for approval/export.
design: Reuse phone_hash + notifications.rate-limiting (Hammer). Payout is finance-gated, never automatic. Fraud signals stored as non-PII projections. Reward config in settings.
acceptance_criteria:
- Referral code/link per user; a referee's completed+won journey marks the referral qualified and computes reward_centimes
- Reward only becomes payable on a gagné/issued policy, never on a mere quote or unverified lead
- Self-referral is blocked via phone_hash/IP matching; velocity caps via Hammer prevent code farming; duplicates flagged for review
- Finance role reviews and approves payouts; approvals are audited and exportable to CSV
- Customer panel shows referral status; amounts in integer centimes MAD
- Tests cover qualify-on-win, self-referral block, velocity cap, and payout gating on policy issuance

title: Build reviews and ratings with moderation and schema.org
description: User reviews build trust and SEO (§2 row 15, §10.8, §8 reviews). Add `Content.Review` (insurer_id nullable, rating 1..5, body, author_name, status pending|approved|rejected, lead_id fk). After a lead transitions to `gagné`, send an invite (SMS/email/WhatsApp) with a tokenized review form. Reviews land pending; ops moderate via an admin queue (approve/reject, reply-as-platform). Approved reviews render on insurer profile pages with aggregate rating and schema.org Review/AggregateRating markup (into the correct place, not duplicated). The public submission changeset must never cast the status field.
design: Admin-only status never cast from user changeset (Lessons). schema.org markup rendered server-side; aggregate recomputed from approved only. Moderation queue lives in admin-studio content area. Invite dedupes per lead.
acceptance_criteria:
- Review schema with rating CHECK 1..5 and status enum; a gagné lead triggers a tokenized review invite
- Public review changeset casts only rating/body/author_name — status is admin-controlled and cannot be forged (test asserts injected status ignored)
- Admin moderation queue lists pending reviews with approve/reject and reply-as-platform; actions are audited
- Approved reviews display on insurer pages with an aggregate rating and valid schema.org Review/AggregateRating JSON-LD
- Rejected/pending reviews never render publicly; aggregate excludes them
- Tests cover invite trigger, status-forgery rejection, moderation transitions, and public visibility filtering

title: Capture CIN at issuance, encrypted and blind-indexed
description: CIN is optional at quote stage but required at policy issuance for the contract (§3.3, §12). Add cloak-encrypted `cin_enc` plus a keyed-HMAC `cin_hash` blind index to the issuance flow (on the policy or user record). Collect CIN in the issuance step with format validation, store encrypted at rest, and expose it only to authorized ops/finance roles in admin, masked by default with an audited reveal. Never log raw CIN and never persist it in plain jsonb. The blind index enables duplicate detection without exposing the value.
design: Follows the phone_enc/phone_hash pattern (Lessons/§12). Reuse security-compliance.cloak-setup vault + HMAC key. Reveal action is an audited admin mutation. Keep CIN out of the quote-stage changeset unless explicitly provided.
acceptance_criteria:
- cin_enc uses cloak AES-GCM; cin_hash is a keyed HMAC (not bare SHA256) enabling lookup/duplicate detection
- CIN is required to complete issuance and validated for format; absent/invalid CIN blocks issuance with a clear error
- Admin reveal of CIN is role-gated, masked by default, and every reveal is written to the audit log
- CIN never appears in logs, telemetry, or plain jsonb payloads
- Duplicate-CIN detection works via the blind index without decrypting
- Tests cover encryption round-trip, hash-based lookup, required-at-issuance enforcement, and audited reveal

title: Deliver e-attestation and track hard-copy logistics
description: Close the buy-online loop by delivering the insurance certificate fast, the way mubi does (§2 row 8, §4 Phase 2). On policy issuance, deliver the e-attestation document by email (Swoosh) and WhatsApp, surface it in the customer panel documents area, and log delivery. Add hard-copy logistics tracking: a `Policies.Shipment` sub-record (carrier, tracking_ref, status pending|sent|delivered) for insurers requiring a physical attestation, manageable from admin. Documents are stored in the private uploads dir and served only through the authenticated ownership-checked controller. Delivery channel selection honours the WhatsApp Business API when enabled, else email + wa.me.
design: Reuse authenticated uploads controller and notifications_log. WhatsApp path defers to phase2.whatsapp-business-api when its flag is on. Store attestation as a private artifact, never a user-controlled path.
acceptance_criteria:
- On issuance the e-attestation is emailed and (when enabled) sent via WhatsApp template; each delivery writes a notifications_log row
- The document appears in the customer panel documents area and downloads only via the authenticated ownership-checked controller
- Policies.Shipment tracks hard-copy carrier/tracking/status; admin can update status and it is audited
- Delivery gracefully degrades to email + wa.me deep link when the Business API flag is off
- Delivery is retryable via Oban with backoff; a permanently failed send raises an ops-visible flag
- Tests cover email delivery, WhatsApp-enabled path, shipment status transitions, and retry

title: Build policies schema and issuance workflow
description: After payment (or agency collection) the platform must issue and track a policy (§7.2 Policies, §4 Phase 2). Add the `Policies` context with a `Policy` schema (user_id, quote_id, insurer_id, product_id, formula, premium_centimes, effect_date, expiry_date, status draft|active|issued|cancelled, external_ref, documents). Build the issuance workflow: on paid payment or ops confirmation, create the policy, mark the linked lead `gagné` with converted_policy_ref + signed premium, and set expiry to feed the renewal engine. Ops can drive issuance from the admin lead detail. Emit PubSub on issuance for admin tiles. Hard-copy logistics tracking (below) attaches here.
design: converted_policy_ref/commission live on leads (§8). Reuse admin-leads.leads-schema. Status transitions audited via foundation.audit-log. PubSub topic policies:* mirrors leads kanban pattern.
acceptance_criteria:
- Policy schema with status enum + CHECK constraints; expiry_date drives renewal reminders; money in integer centimes
- Issuance transitions the linked lead to gagné, records converted_policy_ref and signed premium (calibration input), inside a transaction
- Workflow is triggerable both by successful CMI payment and by manual ops confirmation (agency fallback)
- Admin lead detail exposes an 'issue policy' action guarded by role; all mutations audited
- PubSub event emitted on issuance so admin dashboards update without refresh
- Tests cover payment-triggered issuance, manual issuance, and lead/policy consistency

title: Integrate CMI payment with exactly-once callback
description: Enable online premium payment for binding offers via Morocco's CMI gateway (§11 Payments, §4 Phase 2). Add a `Payments.Gateway` behaviour and `Payments.CMI` adapter: create order, redirect to CMI hosted page, receive the server-to-server callback. Persist `Payments.Session` (order ref, amount_centimes, status). The callback runs through a CSRF-exempt router pipeline, signature is verified IN the Payments context with Plug.Crypto.secure_compare, and status is applied exactly-once inside Repo.transaction (terminal status = no-op). On success, trigger the policy issuance workflow. Always offer a 'payer à l'agence / au conseiller' fallback. Store only non-PII projections of the callback payload. Sandbox config first.
design: Follow the external-provider pattern exactly (Lessons). HTTP via Req/Finch, never hackney. secure_compare, not ==. Terminal-status no-op prevents double issuance. Reconciliation report feeds finance role. Sandbox endpoint via CMI_ENDPOINT env.
acceptance_criteria:
- Payments.Gateway behaviour + CMI adapter; a deterministic Fake gateway is the default in dev/test and secrets come only from runtime.exs env
- Callback route is CSRF-exempt; signature verified with Plug.Crypto.secure_compare in the context; a bad/absent signature is rejected with no state change
- Status transition is exactly-once inside Repo.transaction — a replayed callback on a terminal session is a no-op (test asserts single issuance)
- Successful payment enqueues/triggers policy issuance; failure and timeout are handled; agency-payment fallback path exists and is selectable
- Only safe_raw/1 projections of the callback are persisted — no raw payload in plain jsonb; a reconciliation report lists sessions vs. gateway status for finance
- Whole integration is gated by a settings feature flag; tests cover success, replay, bad-signature, and fallback

title: Introduce Quoting.Source behaviour with binding flag
description: Phase 2 mixes indicative engine prices with live binding quotes from partnered insurers without changing the funnel or results UI (§9.3). Define a `Quoting.Source` behaviour with `@callback quote(inputs) :: {:ok, [Offer.t()]} | {:error, term}`. Ship `RatingEngineSource` (wraps the pure Rating.Engine, default, `binding: false`) plus stub `InsurerAPISource` and `ExtranetSource` scaffolds (Fake implementations for dev/test) selected per-insurer via settings. Add a `binding` boolean to offers; the results page shows the extra 'Souscrire en ligne' CTA only on binding offers (§5.3), otherwise the existing rappel/WhatsApp CTAs. A source resolver merges offers from all enabled sources into one ranked list.
design: Rating engine stays pure; sources are the impure boundary. HTTP adapters use Req/Finch, never hackney. binding CTA is additive — funnel/results layout unchanged per §9.3. Feature-flag each real source in settings.
acceptance_criteria:
- Quoting.Source behaviour defined; RatingEngineSource returns binding:false offers and is the configured default
- offers table gains a binding boolean (default false); migration is version-agnostic and backfills existing rows
- Results page renders 'Souscrire en ligne' CTA only when offer.binding is true; non-binding offers keep rappel/WhatsApp CTAs unchanged
- Source resolver merges + re-ranks offers from multiple enabled sources; per-insurer source is settings-configurable with Fake default
- InsurerAPISource/ExtranetSource have deterministic Fake implementations used in tests; no live HTTP in test
- Tests cover default engine-only path, mixed binding/non-binding ranking, and CTA gating

title: Build echeance-driven renewal reminder sequences
description: The biggest LTV lever: nudge drivers before their contract expires with a one-tap re-quote (§2 row 12, §4 Phase 2). The funnel already captures `current_expiry`. Add an Oban worker `Notifications.RenewalWorker` and a scheduler (Oban Cron daily) that finds quotes/policies with echeance in configurable windows (e.g. J-30, J-15, J-3) and enqueues SMS/email/WhatsApp reminders carrying a deep link that opens a prefilled new devis (reusing saved profile/vehicle). Each reminder is idempotent (one per contact per window), respects marketing-consent and opt-out, and logs to notifications_log. Windows and channels are settings-driven feature flags.
design: echeance = quotes.current_expiry / policies expiry. Africa/Casablanca TZ for date math. Unique Oban args (contact+window) prevent double-sends across runs. WhatsApp channel routes through the Business API task when enabled, else email/SMS.
acceptance_criteria:
- Daily Oban Cron job selects due echeance dates per configurable window and enqueues exactly one reminder per contact per window (idempotent, unique args)
- Reminder deep link opens a new devis prefilled from the user's saved profile/vehicle (or the source quote for anonymous)
- Reminders are suppressed when marketing consent is absent or the user opted out; suppression is logged
- Channel selection (SMS/email/WhatsApp) and windows are read from settings, not hard-coded
- Every send writes a notifications_log row with channel, to_hash, template, status
- Tests cover window selection, idempotency on re-run, and consent/opt-out suppression

title: Build customer panel: quote history, documents, policies
description: The self-service hub that makes the account worth having (§2 row 11, §4 Phase 2). Build `MonCompteLive` under /mon-compte: quote history (list of past tokens with formula, date, offer count, resume/re-quote links), a documents area (devis PDFs, uploaded relevé, later e-attestations served via the authenticated uploads controller — never user-controlled paths), and a policies list once §Policies exists. LiveView streams for lists with count-guarded empty-states OUTSIDE the stream container. Newest-first ordering with a desc: :id tiebreaker. FR/AR + RTL throughout. Documents download through the existing private-dir authenticated controller with ownership checks.
design: Lessons: empty-state outside stream; desc: :id tiebreaker; HEEx uses socket assigns. Reuse the MVP uploads controller, don't build a new file route. Documents area is read-only surfacing of existing artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Quote history renders newest-first on second-precision timestamps using a desc: :id tiebreaker; pagination or capped list
- Empty-state markup sits OUTSIDE the phx-update=stream container, guarded by a @count assign (no LiveViewTest crash)
- Document downloads enforce user ownership via the authenticated uploads controller; a user cannot fetch another user's file (test returns 403/404)
- Panel is fully FR/AR with logical Tailwind utilities (ms/me/ps/pe), dir flips correctly
- Policies section renders gracefully when the user has none
- Tests cover history ordering, empty-state render, and cross-user document access denial

title: Add saved profiles/vehicles with next-quote auto-refill
description: Returning customers should never re-enter their car and driver data — the mubi auto-refill lever (§2 row 11). Add `Accounts.SavedProfile` and `Accounts.SavedVehicle` schemas (belongs_to user), populated on first completed quote and editable from the panel. When a logged-in user starts a new `devis`, prefill the DevisLive embedded step schemas from the most recent saved profile/vehicle, while keeping every field editable (autosave still writes the quote row). Add a boundary function `Accounts.prefill_for(user)` returning a struct the Quoting context maps onto a fresh quote token. Link a completed quote's driver/coverage answers back to the user on login.
design: Snapshots on quotes/rating_runs stay immutable — prefill copies values, never references. Support multiple saved vehicles (one card each, one-tap select). Don't cast admin/internal flags from panel changesets.
acceptance_criteria:
- Completing a quote while authenticated upserts a SavedProfile (driver fields) and SavedVehicle (vehicle fields), PII fields encrypted
- Starting a new devis as a logged-in user prefills steps 1-2 from the latest saved data; all prefilled fields remain editable and re-validate on phx-change
- prefill_for/1 is a pure boundary function returning safe projections; DevisLive calls the context, never the Repo
- A user with no saved data starts an empty funnel with no error
- Editing a saved vehicle in the panel does not retroactively mutate historical quote snapshots
- Tests cover first-quote capture, prefill-on-new-quote, and multi-vehicle selection

title: Build customer accounts: magic-link + OTP login
description: Phase 2 turns anonymous quoters into returning customers so we can hold their book and drive renewals (§4 Phase 2, §2 row 11). Extend the Accounts context with a customer `users` schema (phone_enc/phone_hash, email citext, name, locale) distinct from `admins`. Implement passwordless login: email magic-link (Swoosh, signed Phoenix.Token, 15-min TTL) AND phone OTP reusing the funnel OTP mechanism. Add `UserAuth` plug/hooks, session, `require_authenticated_user` for the customer panel routes, and a `mount_current_user` on_mount. Locale on the user record seeds locale resolution after path/cookie. No admin privileges cross over; separate session key and layout.
design: Reuse funnel.otp-flow primitives, don't fork them. Secrets via runtime.exs env. HEEx reads socket assigns only. Keep admins and users as separate schemas/sessions to avoid privilege bleed. Locale slots into path->cookie->session->user->accept-language order.
acceptance_criteria:
- users table cloak-encrypts phone (phone_enc) with keyed-HMAC phone_hash for lookup; email is citext unique; no bare SHA256
- Magic-link tokens are single-use, expire in 15 min, and a consumed/expired token renders an error not a login
- OTP login reuses hashed-at-rest codes, 5-min TTL, 3 attempts, rate-limited per phone AND per IP; changing the phone field resets verification
- UserAuth on_mount redirects unauthenticated visitors away from /mon-compte routes; admins cannot authenticate as customers and vice-versa
- user changeset never casts admin-only fields; test asserts a forged is_active/role param is ignored
- Tests cover magic-link happy path, expired token, OTP wrong-code lockout, and session fixation on login

title: Start own intermediary agrement track in parallel
description: §1 and §15 recommend launching under a partner courtier while pursuing our own ACAPS intermediary agrement in parallel (Law 17-99 art. 289/306) to reduce dependency on the partner. Start the own-agrement track: eligibility review, exam and conditions, capital/entity requirements and timeline; assign an owner and document milestones. This is non-blocking for MVP launch — it runs alongside the broker path.
design: Refs §1, §15. Launch under (a), pursue (b). Parallel and non-blocking. Business/legal.
acceptance_criteria:
- Agrement requirements and timeline are documented (exam, conditions, entity/capital).
- An owner is assigned and the first application step is initiated.
- A gap analysis of the current entity versus requirements is captured with next actions.

title: Phase 2: Buy online — accounts, payments, renewals, new verticals
description: The full mubi experience once partnerships exist (§4 Phase 2, §9.3): customer accounts (magic-link + OTP) with saved profiles/vehicles and auto-refill, quote history + documents, échéance-driven renewal reminders, the Quoting.Source behaviour adding binding per-insurer quotes, CMI online payment (hosted page, signature-verified exactly-once callbacks, reconciliation, agency fallback), policy issuance + e-attestation delivery, encrypted CIN at issuance, reviews with moderation, referral/cashback with fraud controls, moto and travel (Schengen) verticals via the add-a-line pattern, WhatsApp Business API templates, and the ACAPS full online-subscription dossier filed BEFORE launch.
acceptance_criteria: First binding insurer sellable end-to-end (pay → policy by email in minutes) behind a feature flag; renewals measurably re-engage; each vertical reuses the funnel/results machinery.

title: Phase 3 kickoff gate: Phase 2 proven
description: Phase 3 expansion (habitation, sante, vie, B2B fleet, insurer APIs, PWA, white-label) only starts once Phase 2 has proven out: online payment live with at least one binding insurer, renewals measurably re-engaging, and the moto/travel add-a-line pattern validated. This gate blocks all Phase 3 issues until that evidence exists. Closing it is a deliberate product decision — record which Phase 3 bets are being taken and why.
design: Keeps the backlog honest: Phase 3 tasks are scoping placeholders until this gate opens them.
acceptance_criteria:
- Phase 2 buy-online live with >= 1 binding insurer
- renewal reminders showing measurable re-engagement
- add-a-line pattern validated by moto/travel in production
- chosen Phase 3 scope and rationale recorded on close

title: Add white-label mode for banks/dealerships
description: Enable partner-branded deployments for banks/dealerships with attribution (§4 Phase 3). Add a `Partners` context (partner slug, theme tokens, logo, contact, active) and a partner-resolution plug (subdomain or path) that overrides design tokens/logo/legal footer per partner while reusing the same funnel/engine. Tag every quote/lead with partner attribution for reporting and commission split. Partner theming overrides tokens at the layout root; falls back to default brand when no partner matches. Admin manages partners; attribution surfaces in exports.
design: Theme via CSS custom properties overriding design-system.tokens at the root. Attribution is a projection on quotes/leads for commission split. Admin-only partner flags never user-cast (Lessons). No hardcoded brand — everything token/settings-driven.
acceptance_criteria:
- Partners schema + resolution plug (subdomain/path) selects a partner and applies its theme/logo/legal footer at the layout root
- Quotes and leads are tagged with partner attribution; exports and reports break down by partner
- Theming overrides design tokens per partner and falls back cleanly to the default brand when unmatched
- Partner CRUD in admin is role-gated and audited; is_active/published-style flags never cast from any public changeset
- FR + AR and RTL preserved under partner themes
- Tests cover partner resolution, attribution tagging, theme fallback, and export breakdown

title: Add PWA polish: manifest, offline shell, add-to-home
description: Improve mobile stickiness with a PWA layer (or decide on a thin app) per §4 Phase 3. Add a web app manifest (name from settings/gettext — no hardcoded brand), icons, theme colors matching design tokens, an add-to-home prompt, and a minimal service worker providing an offline shell for static/content routes (never caching authenticated or quote-sensitive data). Respect prefers-reduced-motion and the <120KB JS budget. Document the thin-app decision as a short recommendation.
design: No hardcoded brand strings (Phase 0 name from settings). Never cache PII/authenticated responses — security over convenience. Keep the service worker minimal; LiveView needs the network anyway. Icons reuse the zellige-star motif.
acceptance_criteria:
- Valid manifest with icons/theme colors from design tokens; app display name resolved from settings/gettext, not hardcoded
- Add-to-home works on Android/iOS Safari; installability audit passes
- Service worker caches only static/content shell; authenticated and quote/PII routes are never cached
- JS budget stays under 120KB; prefers-reduced-motion respected
- A short written thin-app-vs-PWA recommendation is recorded
- Tests/audit confirm manifest validity and no caching of authenticated routes

title: Build per-insurer API/extranet integration framework
description: As partnerships appear, generalize the Phase 2 Quoting.Source scaffolds into a robust per-insurer integration framework (§9.3, §4 Phase 3). Formalize InsurerAPISource/ExtranetSource with per-insurer config (endpoints, auth, field mapping), resilient HTTP (Req/Finch, timeouts, retries, circuit-breaking), response normalization to Offer structs with binding:true, and per-insurer health/telemetry. Each integration is settings-flagged and falls back to the rating engine on failure so the results page never breaks. Deterministic Fakes for dev/test.
design: Builds directly on phase2.quoting-source-behaviour. Never hackney; Req/Finch only. Fallback-to-engine keeps the UI resilient (§9.3 unchanged UI). Circuit-breaking protects the funnel from partner outages.
acceptance_criteria:
- A reusable adapter contract lets a new insurer be added via config + a mapping module, no core changes
- HTTP is resilient (Req/Finch timeouts, bounded retries, circuit-break); a slow/failing insurer degrades to engine offers without breaking results
- Live responses normalize to Offer structs with binding:true and feed the source resolver ranking
- Each integration is settings-flagged with a deterministic Fake default; no live HTTP in tests
- Per-insurer telemetry (latency, error rate, fallback count) is emitted
- Tests cover normalization, timeout/fallback, and multi-source ranking with a live-style Fake

title: Build B2B fleet quote flow
description: Fleet (parc auto) quoting serves businesses with multiple vehicles (§4 Phase 3). Build a B2B flow allowing entry of multiple vehicles per request (bulk add or CSV), company details, and a consolidated fleet quote request that produces an aggregated estimate and a specialized high-priority lead for the ops/agent team. Reuse the auto rating engine per-vehicle and sum, plus a fleet positioning factor from rate_tables. Distinct source/segment in the leads workspace. FR + AR.
design: Reuse Rating.Engine per vehicle; fleet factor is a table value, not code. Uploads follow the private-dir/content-sniff rules (Lessons/§12). High-priority routing in the existing kanban.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fleet request accepts multiple vehicles (bulk add and/or CSV upload) plus company details
- Per-vehicle rating reuses the pure engine; a fleet positioning factor from rate_tables adjusts the aggregate
- The flow creates a high-priority B2B lead with a distinct source, carrying the vehicle list snapshot
- CSV upload is validated (size-capped, content sniffed) and served via safe handling, never user paths
- Flow is FR + AR with RTL-correct layout
- Tests cover multi-vehicle aggregation, fleet factor application, and lead creation

title: Add vie/epargne lead-gen to advisors
description: Life/savings (vie/epargne) is advisory-heavy, so Phase 3 does lead-gen rather than instant quoting (§2 row 19, §4 Phase 3). Build a lightweight qualification form (goals, horizon, capacity, contact) that creates a specialized lead routed to advisor agents in the existing admin leads workspace (a distinct source/segment). No rating engine offers page — the outcome is a qualified advisor lead with OTP-verified contact. FR + AR. Reuse leads schema, OTP, and kanban.
design: Reuse admin-leads pipeline + OTP; this is a funnel-light lead capture, not a quoting vertical. Keep it a thin variant, not a new context.
acceptance_criteria:
- A vie/epargne qualification form captures goals/horizon/capacity + OTP-verified contact and creates a lead tagged with a distinct source
- Leads route to advisor agents in the existing kanban with correct segment filtering
- No offers/rating path is invoked; the flow ends at a confirmed advisor lead
- Consent capture (text version/timestamp/IP) matches the MVP consent pattern
- Form is fully FR + AR with RTL layout
- Tests cover lead creation, source tagging, and OTP verification reuse

title: Add sante complementaire (mutuelle) vertical
description: Complementary health (mutuelle) is a high-demand vertical (§2 row 19, §4 Phase 3). Add sante products (kind=sante), sante rate_tables (age bands, coverage tier, family composition), and a sante funnel variant of DevisLive reusing step components. Given the sensitivity, collect the minimum necessary data and treat any health-adjacent fields as sensitive (no unnecessary PII, consent-first). Offers, OTP, lead capture, and admin flow unchanged. FR + AR labels for all fields. Reuse the Quoting.Source resolver.
design: Phase-3 vertical bundled end-to-end via add-a-line. Health data sensitivity: minimize + consent-first, encrypt anything PII, no raw payloads in jsonb. Engine remains pure/table-driven.
acceptance_criteria:
- kind=sante products + versioned sante rate_tables authored in the rating studio
- Sante funnel variant reuses step components with age/composition/tier inputs and one-tap cards
- Only minimal necessary data collected; any sensitive field is consent-gated and not persisted in plain jsonb
- Sante quotes create leads and reuse offers/OTP/admin unchanged
- All fields have FR + AR labels with RTL-correct layout
- Tests cover sante rating from tables, funnel completion, and minimal-data enforcement

title: Add habitation (home) insurance vertical
description: Home insurance expands the book beyond mobility (§2 row 19, §4 Phase 3). Following the add-a-line pattern proven by moto/travel, add habitation products (kind=habitation), habitation rate_tables (surface, rooms, contents value, city risk zone, coverage level), and a habitation funnel variant of DevisLive reusing step components. Offers, OTP, lead capture, and admin all flow through unchanged. Seed a minimal catalog and author FR + AR labels for all new fields. Reuse the Quoting.Source resolver so binding integrations attach later.
design: Coarse phase-3 vertical bundled end-to-end. Reuse the moto/travel add-a-line scaffolding; engine stays table-driven and pure. Author FR + AR catalogs, no empty msgids.
acceptance_criteria:
- kind=habitation products + versioned habitation rate_tables authored in the rating studio
- Habitation funnel variant reuses step components; one-tap option cards for small enums; date/number validation
- Rating.Engine computes habitation offers purely from tables (no business numbers in code)
- Habitation quotes create leads and reuse offers/OTP/admin unchanged
- All new fields have FR + AR gettext labels with RTL-correct layout
- Tests cover habitation rating, funnel completion, and lead parity

title: Phase 3: Expansion
description: Post-PMF growth options (§4 Phase 3), deliberately coarse until Phase 2 proves out: habitation and santé complémentaire verticals, vie/épargne lead-gen to advisors, B2B fleet quoting, a per-insurer API/extranet integration framework as partnerships appear, PWA polish or thin-app decision, and white-label mode for banks/dealerships. Each becomes its own epic when scheduled — these tasks are placeholders with enough context to scope later.
acceptance_criteria: Each item has a scoping note sufficient to expand into a full epic without re-reading the market context.

Sahla plan filed 2026-07-02 from docs/fplansahla.md: 17 epics / 184 tasks / 475 blocking deps. Orientation map + conventions: docs/implementation-plan.md; slug->id map: docs/build-plan-id-map.json. Build order = 6 milestone gates (bd list -l gate, sahla-jxp.9..14): M1 foundation, M2 catalog+funnel 1-3, M3 quote-to-lead spine, M4 admin, M5 public site+i18n+hardening, M6 launch go/no-go. Phase 2/3 hard-gated behind phase2/phase3 gate-kickoff issues - do not close mechanically. Engineering never blocks on business tasks: rating uses placeholder grids until phase0.rate-grids delivers broker baremes via the rating studio. Follow-up sahla-jxp.15: adversarial completeness re-check of the plan vs spec (original critics died on session limit).

Sahla.CSV (lib/sahla/csv.ex) is the shared, dependency-free RFC-4180-subset CSV parser (comma delimiter, double-quote quoting + "" escapes, LF/CRLF, blank-line skip; NO embedded newlines in quotes). Used by Sahla.Directory.Import (product/guarantee matrix, ni1.8) and Sahla.Vehicles.Import (vehicle catalog, ni1.7). Import pattern for both: import_csv/1 -> import_rows/1; each row upserted in its own Repo.transaction by natural key (find-or-create), row-level errors collected into summary %{...created, ...inserted, ...updated, failed, errors:[%{row,error}]}, bad rows skipped not fatal, idempotent re-run. Oban workers live under <Context>.Workers.* on queue :imports, delegate to Import, return {:ok, summary}, CSV passed inline in job args. FUTURE CSV import tasks (e.g. rating-csv-import 8y3.3, leads/quotes exports) should REUSE Sahla.CSV — do NOT add NimbleCSV without asking (specs suggest it but the subset parser suffices). Persisted import-report table deferred (returned summary only).
